data: Equity What would be the impact on health equity?

○ Reduced No research evidence searched for. The GDG considered the treatment duration and ○ Probably the ability to decentralize treatment (to enable reduced access for remote, underserviced settings and ○ Probably no disadvantaged populations) to affect equity. impact The GDG highlighted that health equity would ● Probably probably increase given parts of the population increased that would have access to the shorter regimen ○ Increased and the medications included, in particular ○ Varies pregnant women and children and this may apply ○ Don’t know to other groups as well. On the other hand, it was also noted that there are populations that might not be able to afford the regimen, and between- country differences in impact on health equity may exist because of availability of medications. Voting for a decision on the judgement took place: • 13 GDG members voted ‘probably increased’ • 3 GDG member voted ‘increased’ Despite not being able to identify relevant research evidence, the panel used their collective experience to judge that there would likely be advantages associated with the use of the BDLLfxC regimen due to its reduced complexity and shorter duration. The panel judged that use of the BDLLfxC regimen would probably increase equity.
